(don't use) ```lua vim.pack.add({ { src = "https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim" }, { src = "https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim" }, { src = "https://github.com/folke/tokyonight.nvim" }, { src = "https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter", version = "main" }, }) vim.cmd.colorscheme("tokyonight") -- require("nvim-treesitter").install({ "lua" }) -- vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("FileType", { -- desc = "Setup treesitter for a buffer", -- pattern = { "lua" }, -- group = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("ts_setup", { clear = true }), -- callback = function(e) -- vim.treesitter.start(e.buf) -- end, -- }) require("mini.pick").setup() vim.keymap.set("n", "sg", ":Pick grep_live", { desc = "Search grep" }) local H = require("snacks.picker.util.highlight") local get_highlights = function(code, ft, offset) local highlights = H.get_highlights({ code = code, ft = ft })[1] for _, hl in ipairs(highlights) do hl.col = hl.col + offset hl.end_col = hl.end_col + offset end return highlights end local ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("pick_grep") MiniPick.default_show_ts = function(buf_id, data, query, opts) vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf_id, ns, 0, -1) local items = {} local lines = {} for _, dt in ipairs(data) do local file, row, col, code = unpack(vim.split(dt, "%z")) local ft = vim.filetype.match({ filename = file }) local prepend = string.format("%s:%d:%d ", file, row, col) local highlights = {} local row_start, row_end = string.find(prepend, row, #file + 1) local col_start, col_end = string.find(prepend, col, row_end + 1) vim.list_extend(highlights, { { col = row_start - 1, end_col = row_end, hl_group = "Conceal", priority = 100 }, { col = col_start - 1, end_col = col_end, hl_group = "Added", priority = 100 }, }) vim.list_extend(highlights, get_highlights(code, ft, #prepend)) local item = { text = prepend .. code, highlights = highlights, } table.insert(items, item) table.insert(lines, item.text) end vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf_id, 0, -1, true, lines) for i, item in ipairs(items) do for _, extm in ipairs(item.highlights) do local row, col = i - 1, extm.col extm.col = nil local ok, err = pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark, buf_id, ns, row, col, extm) if not ok then vim.notify(err, vim.log.levels.ERROR) end end end end MiniPick.registry.grep_live = function(local_opts, opts) return MiniPick.builtin.grep_live( local_opts, vim.tbl_deep_extend("keep", opts or {}, { source = { show = MiniPick.default_show_ts, }, }) ) end ```
If `mini.nvim` had a function similar to [H.get_highlights](https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim/blob/fe7cfe9800a182274d0f868a74b7263b8c0c020b/lua/snacks/picker/util/highlight.lua#L25-L110) from [snacks.nvim](https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim), adding syntax highlighting to the `grep` picker would be relatively easy. It could be under `misc` or `extra`. Am I missing something? Is there already a way to do so?

Related:

  • #2152

This is a proof of concept:

Caution

This code relies on snacks.nvim. Don’t use it.

Caution

No match highlighting.
No caching.

Note

Doesn’t highlight multiline if statements in Lua.

if true then
end
(don't use) 
vim.pack.add({
  { src = "https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim" },
  { src = "https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim" },
  { src = "https://github.com/folke/tokyonight.nvim" },
  { src = "https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter", version = "main" },
})

vim.cmd.colorscheme("tokyonight")

-- require("nvim-treesitter").install({ "lua" })
-- vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("FileType", {
--   desc = "Setup treesitter for a buffer",
--   pattern = { "lua" },
--   group = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("ts_setup", { clear = true }),
--   callback = function(e)
--     vim.treesitter.start(e.buf)
--   end,
-- })

require("mini.pick").setup()
vim.keymap.set("n", "<Space>sg", ":Pick grep_live<CR>", { desc = "Search grep" })

local H = require("snacks.picker.util.highlight")
local get_highlights = function(code, ft, offset)
  local highlights = H.get_highlights({ code = code, ft = ft })[1]
  for _, hl in ipairs(highlights) do
    hl.col = hl.col + offset
    hl.end_col = hl.end_col + offset
  end
  return highlights
end

local ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("pick_grep")
MiniPick.default_show_ts = function(buf_id, data, query, opts)
  vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf_id, ns, 0, -1)
  local items = {}
  local lines = {}
  for _, dt in ipairs(data) do
    local file, row, col, code = unpack(vim.split(dt, "%z"))
    local ft = vim.filetype.match({ filename = file })
    local prepend = string.format("%s:%d:%d ", file, row, col)
    local highlights = {}
    local row_start, row_end = string.find(prepend, row, #file + 1)
    local col_start, col_end = string.find(prepend, col, row_end + 1)
    vim.list_extend(highlights, {
      { col = row_start - 1, end_col = row_end, hl_group = "Conceal", priority = 100 },
      { col = col_start - 1, end_col = col_end, hl_group = "Added", priority = 100 },
    })
    vim.list_extend(highlights, get_highlights(code, ft, #prepend))
    local item = {
      text = prepend .. code,
      highlights = highlights,
    }
    table.insert(items, item)
    table.insert(lines, item.text)
  end
  vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf_id, 0, -1, true, lines)
  for i, item in ipairs(items) do
    for _, extm in ipairs(item.highlights) do
      local row, col = i - 1, extm.col
      extm.col = nil
      local ok, err = pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark, buf_id, ns, row, col, extm)
      if not ok then
        vim.notify(err, vim.log.levels.ERROR)
      end
    end
  end
end

MiniPick.registry.grep_live = function(local_opts, opts)
  return MiniPick.builtin.grep_live(
    local_opts,
    vim.tbl_deep_extend("keep", opts or {}, {
      source = {
        show = MiniPick.default_show_ts,
      },
    })
  )
end

If mini.nvim had a function similar to H.get_highlights from snacks.nvim, adding syntax highlighting to the grep picker would be relatively easy. It could be under misc or extra.

Am I missing something? Is there already a way to do so?

comment_data.body:
Thanks for sharing!

> This code relies on [snacks.nvim](https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim). Don’t use it.

To be perfectly honest, if an advice is to *not* use it, then here is probably not the best place to post.

> If `mini.nvim` had a function similar to [H.get_highlights](https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim/blob/fe7cfe9800a182274d0f868a74b7263b8c0c020b/lua/snacks/picker/util/highlight.lua#L25-L110) from [snacks.nvim](https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim), adding syntax highlighting to the `grep` picker would be relatively easy. It could be under `misc` or `extra`.

I think the correct place for this kind of thing is Neovim core. I think there would be an interest in having *some variant* of this under `vim.treesitter`. But only if somebody is willing to go through making a issue+PR on top of back-and-fourth discussions about scope/implementation.

---

Also, couple of quick notes:

- Please, don't recommend solutions that monkey-patch global `MiniXxx` tables. The `MiniPick.default_show_ts` can be `local default_show_ts`.
- If you share useful code snippets here, please make them as minimal and 'mini.nvim' related as possible. For example, there is no need to install 'tokyonight.nvim' in the example. Probably, the same goes for 'nvim-treesitter' (just a mention of set up tree-sitter highlighting is enough).
